properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 14 at 3:00PM MDT until August 14 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 300 PM MDT, Pueblo doppler radar indicated the heavies rain has
moved off of the Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. However, radar
estimates 3/4 to 1 and a half inches of rain has fallen over the past
two hours, with flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris
flow moving through the Middle Creek and North Creek Drainages. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
San Isabel, Highway 165, Beulah, Highway 78, stream crossings, and
county roads within and immediately downstream of the burn scar.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 14 at 2:59PM MDT until August 14 at 3:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 259 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Byers, or 36
miles east of Denver, moving northeast at 5 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Bennett, Byers and Strasburg.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 14 at 2:59PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 259 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Englewood, or 7 miles south of Denver, moving north at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around

possible.

Locations impacted include...
Denver, western Aurora, eastern Lakewood, Centennial, northeastern
Highlands Ranch, Littleton, Englewood, Greenwood Village, Lone
Tree, Sheridan, Buckley SFB, Cherry Hills Village, Edgewater,
Mountain View, Cherry Creek Reservoir, Columbine and Ken Caryl.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 14 at 2:57PM MDT until August 14 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
FFWBOU

The National Weather Service in Denver has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Adams County in northeastern Colorado...
Central Arapahoe and Eastern Arapahoe County in northeastern
Colorado...

* Until 600 PM MDT.

* At 257 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
0.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
up to 1.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches,
roads, and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Byers and Strasburg.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Mule Creek, Muddy Creek, Little Comanche Creek, Comanche Creek,
Rattlesnake Creek, Bijou Creek, Sherman Ranch Slough, Little
Antelope Creek, Wolf Creek, East Bijou Creek, Antelope Creek and
West Bijou Creek.

properties.description:

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 14 at 2:46PM MDT until August 14 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Elbert County in east central Colorado...
Arapahoe County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry creeks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 246 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. This may cause small
stream flooding. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Gold Creek, Running Creek, Little Comanche Creek, Dry Creek,
Comanche Creek, Little Dry Creek, Wolf Creek, Kiowa Creek and
West Bijou Creek. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches
are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in
minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bennett and Elizabeth.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 14 at 2:41PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 240 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 9
miles northeast of Sugarite Canyon State Park, or 13 miles southeast
of Trinidad, moving east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph, pea size hail and torrential
rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible. Heavy rain will cause ponding of water on
roadways and quick rises in area creeks, streams and
normally dry washes.

Locations impacted include...
Trinchera.
